stem:
Ekta presses a rubber sucker onto a smooth steel cupboard. After she pushes air out from under the sucker, it stays firmly in place.

Why does the sucker stick?

options.text: The air pressure outside the sucker is greater than the air pressure under it, so the outside air presses it against the steel.
The atmospheric pressure outside sticks the sucker to the steel even when air was not pushed out from under it.
The air pressure under the sucker is greater than the air pressure outside, so the inside air presses it against the steel.
The sucker sticks even when the air pressure outside equals the air pressure under it.

teacher.key_rationale: Pushing air out lowers pressure under the sucker; higher outside atmospheric pressure presses it onto the steel. B applies air-pressure sticking without the lowered inside pressure. C reverses which side has higher pressure. D drops the need for a pressure difference.
